questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: French people had told me a lot of good things about Tours + affordable living costs + I wanted to speak French, so I didn't want a big, international city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing. So many new impressions, nice people and great things to do, I really needed that after almost two years of covid

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I arrived a couple of weeks before the semester started, so I had a lot of time to figure it all out. It was quite easy to find information, the university of Tours sent out emails with the most basic stuff and adresses, deadlines etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any assistance from the university, but my housemates in Tours picked me up at the train station and helped me a lot in the beginning

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The whole uni inscription, welcome meetings etc were a bit chaotic and many informations at once. A lot of paperwork and it took a few hours a couple of times (also keeping in mind documents and signatures for KU), but it worked out fine in the end

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found a room in a great flatshare in Facebook group. It's much, much easier and cheaper than in Copenhagen. I did it before moving to France, but it's definitely doable   upon arrival as well

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Good if you want to speak French and get to know French people. Might be a bit more expensive than student residences, but not much, and it'll usually already be equipped with pots and pans etc that you won't find in residences.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't live in a student residence, but I visited often and they seemed somewhat decent, depending on the residence. The rooms are a bit small though and there's no kitchen equipment at all, no oven in the common kitchen etc., so you'll have to bring or buy stuff there. The student residences aren't as social as Danish student residences tend to be, so you don't get to speak much French there. On the other hand, there's often a big group of Erasmus people living there too which is nice too

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult. Not all courses were listed in the online course catalogue and it wasn't updated for the semester either, it was hard to find course descriptions for the pre-approval at KU, and it was a puzzle to put together my timetable without having overlapping classes or too little time for moving between different campuses. There was a lot of emailing back and forth with my coordinator, following courses and dropping them again before finally having a finished timetable a few weeks into the semester

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: See above

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a lovely coordinator, Carine, who helped me a lot

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat succesful. I couldn't make it work with all of the classes that I wanted, but I found good replacements

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It's normal if the registration process is chaotic and takes a lot of time, it's the same for all the exchange students. Don't worry if you don't get all the courses you want and be prepared to change
classes.The
university administration in Tours is generally helpful and patient. Make sure also to talk to your coordinator at KU to help with pre-approval and paperwork for KU

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I followed courses in all three years of the bachelor's level. In general, I find the level a bit lower than at KU, but it depends a lot on the course. It seems like it's an extension of secondary school at times

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Different. It depends A LOT on the teacher, but in general, it's much more one-way-communication. Especially in lectures, but also in class sessions. Learning things by heart is important, there's less discussion in class than in Denmark. It's not always easy to follow a class if the teacher is talking for two hours straight in French without any kind of powerpoint or writing on the blackboard. Also, class attendance is mandatory and may have an impact on your grade

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction à la sociologie
Théories sociologiques
De la cité à l'urbain 
Creative writing

Expression écrite et orale en français
La littérature, la société et les arts aujourd'hui : l'image et la littérature
Langue écrite universitaire C1
Culture et société B2/C1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Creative writing
Introduction à la sociologie

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I had to buy a housing insurance (one time payment for a year) which is mandatory in France
Transportation fee is low because I bought a second hand bike when I got there

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is a little bit cheaper than in Denmark, especially if you go to the market. Train tickets are quite expensive if you want to take trips to other places in France. Books are much cheaper than in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's a really good sports organisation called SUAPS as a part of uni. They offer sports activities and organise trips to other places: hiking in Bretagne, visiting Mont St Michel, skiing etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A LOT of different activities: bouldering, dance classes, tennis, swimming with SUAPS and it costs almost nothing compared to Denmark. I know that the university offers different kinds of workshops and extracurricular activities as well

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely sports classes, but also festivals, film clubs, theatre etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Mont St Michel, Nantes, Paris, kayaking on the Loire, seeing the castles in the area. In the longer breaks there's a bit more time to travel, so maybe Toulouse or Bordeaux there

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. It helps a lot if you speak some French though

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do Tandem language exchanges for meeting French people. Involve yourself in sports or other activities, talk to people in class and don't be afraid to talk to strangers. Try to become friends with other people's French friends if you can

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It took a little while to get used to the school system + remembering saying 'vous' instead of 'tu' + French bureaucracy

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the language, the books, the people ... it's been great almost all of it

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for paperwork
Enjoy that you're in France and that you're doing an exchange - uni is important, but it's just as important to meet the other exchange students and discover the city
Try to speak French even though you think that you make a lot of mistakes, most people are nice and patient

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's all a bit confusing and stressful in the beginning, but it will be fine after a few weeks

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: How much my French has improved + all the great people I met and the things we did together

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Fitting in the school system and navigating covid, wearing masks all the time etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
